issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency for the loop-end label: the problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 21-22) instructs students to mark the end of the main loop with the label 'loop_end'. The template (template_repository/helloWorld.asm lines 11-18) contains the main code region but does not include any loop-end label. The solution (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm line 17) defines the label 'end_loop' instead of 'loop_end'. This mismatch can confuse students about which exact label to add and can cause automated checks that look for the literal 'loop_end' to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the label name consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the label in solution_repository/helloWorld.asm from 'end_loop' to 'loop_end' (change the label on line 17) and add a placeholder 'loop_end:' label in template_repository/helloWorld.asm at the intended location near the end of main (for example, before the 'ret' instruction). Alternatively, change the problem statement to request 'end_loop' and then add that exact label to the template and solution. Ensure template, solution, and problem statement use the same identifier.

issues.description: Label naming for the end of the main loop is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement explicitly requires the loop-end label to be named `loop_end`, the template's main function (helloWorld.asm) is the location where that label is expected/should be added (no `loop_end` present in the template), but the reference solution uses the label `end_loop`. A student following the problem text and the template would expect to add or look for `loop_end`, while the solution uses `end_loop`, causing a mapping mismatch and unnecessary confusion when comparing their code to the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the label name consistent. Rename the solution label `end_loop:` to `loop_end:` in solution_repository/helloWorld.asm (change line with `end_loop:` to `loop_end:`), or alternatively update the problem statement to require `end_loop` -> `end_loop` everywhere. Prefer changing the solution to `loop_end:` so it matches the problem statement and the expected student action.
